description: Dull brown plates shut on a copper vein, far too heavy for its size. A Puddling's last piece; in armour, hard to shift.
lore: This is the one they put in a new hand. It is the plainest hard piece there is, dull brown plates shut against each other, black seams between them, one thread of copper down in the middle taking whatever light is going, and it does the single thing that settles the matter for somebody who has never held one: it weighs wrong. Not heavy. Wrongly heavy, in a way the arm reports before the eye will agree to it. Very little explaining is needed after that.

In armour it does something the low country long ago stopped remarking on. The plate thickens, which anybody can measure. The rest cannot be felt while it is happening: the wearer is not braced, does not feel rooted to anything, and simply finds out afterwards that the blow which should have put them on their back left them standing where they had been standing. People who have worn one for years call it the least dramatic advantage available anywhere, and go on wearing it.

The trouble with them is how many there are, and it is the low-country sorters who have to hold the trouble. Every hard piece is supposed to be the bottom of one long forgetting, one thing thinned all the way down over a great while, and there are more of these coming out of the wet ground than there are lives in the district to account for them, by a margin that gets worse every season. Three explanations are in circulation. That the ground is doing the forgetting and the low wet places are only where it runs deepest. That the counting was always sloppy. And a third, said late in the evening and not repeated in daylight, which is that the arithmetic is fine and it is the assumption of one life to one stone that is wrong.

Meet the creature and you learn very little, there being famously nothing in it to learn. The stone is the only part of the business that holds still long enough to be looked at properly, and what it has to say is not about a life at all. It says that something down in that wet ground was agreed on, by a great many people, for a very long time, and pressed. Loose remembering does not come out this heavy. Whatever else about them is unsettled, that much is in the hand.
